title: Comparatives and superlatives
subtitle: Comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs; so, such, enough, too

rows.use: regular adjectives with one syllable · black
regular adjectives with one syllable (ending in vowel + consonant) · thin
rows.example: double final letter + **-er**: **thinner** · double final letter + **-est**: **thinnest**

rows.use: regular adjectives with two syllables (ending in -y) · funny
regular adjectives with two or more syllables · intelligent
rows.example: **more / less** + adj: **more intelligent** · **most / least** + adj: **most intelligent**
good → **better / best** · bad → **worse / worst** · far → **farther/further / farthest/furthest** · little → **less / least** · much/many → **more / most**

rows.use: Comparative · to compare things or people that are different
rows.example: The crime rate in this area is **higher** than in other parts of the country.

rows.use: Superlative · to compare one member of a group with the whole group
rows.example: The robbery was **the biggest** in the bank's history.

blocks.text: Regular adjectives with two syllables can often also form the comparative and superlative like adjectives with one syllable.

items: Adjectives with one syllable that end in **-e** add **-r** and **-st**: **white, whiter, whitest**
Remember that comparative forms are often followed by **than**: Crime is a much **bigger** problem in this country **than** in many other countries.
Remember that superlative forms are often preceded by **the**: Our local police force is **the best** in the country.

rows.example: comparative: **more / less + adv** · **more easily** · superlative: **most / least + adv** · **most easily**

badly → **worse / worst** · early → **earlier / earliest** · far → **farther/further / farthest/furthest** · fast → **faster / fastest** · hard → **harder / hardest** · late → **later / latest** · often → **more often / most often** · near → **nearer / nearest** · soon → **sooner / soonest** · well → **better / best**
Lock your door **more carefully** next time and maybe you won't get burgled!
Only the criminal who ran **fastest** managed to escape from the police.

rows.use: To show the results of a situation or action
rows.example: The burglar was **so clever that** no one could catch him. · Jane took the money **so quickly that** no one saw her. · There was **so much money that** the robber couldn't carry it all.

blocks.text: The word **that** is not usually necessary to introduce the second clause.
blocks.note: The crime rate is **so high** people are very frightened.

blocks.text: The word **so** has a number of other uses. Try not to get confused between them.
blocks.note: The crime rate is so high **that** people are very frightened. · I saw that burglar leaving the house, **so** I called the police.

blocks.text: Form: **such** + a/an + adjective + singular noun + **that** · **such** + adjective + plural noun + **that** · **such** + a lot of + noun + **that**

rows.use: To show the results of a situation or action
rows.example: It was **such a terrible crime that** the man was sent to prison for life. · The security guard had **such good hearing that** he heard the door open immediately. · There is **such a lot of crime here that** the police can't cope.

blocks.text: Form: **enough** + noun (+ **for** and/or + full infinitive) · adjective + **enough** (+ **for** and/or + full infinitive) · adverb + **enough** (+ **for** and/or + full infinitive)

rows.use: To show the results of a situation or action where there is/isn't the right amount/number of something
rows.example: There aren't **enough** police officers on the streets to keep us safe. · It wasn't dark **enough** for the burglar to start working. · Did the police respond quickly **enough** to help?

blocks.correct: It's **quite / fairly dangerous** around here so don't go out alone.
blocks.incorrect: It's **enough dangerous** around here so don't go out alone.

blocks.text: Form: **too** + adjective (+ **for** and/or + full infinitive) · **too** + adverb (+ **for** and/or + full infinitive) · **too** + many/much + noun (+ **for** and/or + full infinitive)

rows.use: To describe something that is more than necessary and which has a negative effect
rows.example: The young man was **too young** to go to prison. · We arrived **too late** for the start of the trial. · We send **too many** innocent people to prison.

blocks.correct: You were **very / really / extremely lucky** not to get caught.
blocks.incorrect: You were **too lucky** not to get caught.

blocks.text: We do not use **too** when we want to describe something we consider to be positive. Instead, we use **very, really** or **extremely**.

exercises.title: A · Comparatives
exercises.instruction: Complete using the comparative forms of the words in capitals.

items.prompt: Your brother is much ___ (TALL) than mine.
This island used to be much ___ (GREEN) before the forest fires.
Slow down! You're ___ (FIT) than me and I can't keep up!
Veronica seems ___ (HAPPY) since she moved schools.
It's actually ___ (TRENDY) to wear your hair up this year.
As the time for the performance got nearer, I got ___ (NERVOUS).
Old people are often ___ (WISE) than young people.
Why don't you try and find a ___ (CHEAP) computer game and save some money?
Matt seems to have got even ___ (LAZY) than he used to be and almost never studies.
If the problem gets any ___ (SERIOUS), we may need to inform the manager about it.
If you work ___ (QUICKLY), you'll finish sooner and then you can go home earlier.
Ben says he's feeling much ___ (WELL) after his illness.
I have even ___ (LITTLE) free time this year than I did last year.
The news was much ___ (BAD) than anyone had feared.
You'll need to be able to run ___ (FAR) than this if you're going to do the marathon.

exercises.title: B · Superlatives
exercises.instruction: Complete using the superlative forms of the words in capitals.

items.prompt: I think Mohammed Ali was the ___ (GREAT) boxer that ever lived.
It was the ___ (BORING) film I had ever seen.
Our teacher told us that the student with the ___ (HIGH) mark would get a prize.
Ginger is one of the ___ (LUCKY) cats alive — he's been hit by a car three times and has never been hurt!
Out of all the students in my music school, I practise ___ (OFTEN).
The Pacific is the ___ (DEEP) ocean in the world.
That's the ___ (UGLY) fish I've ever seen!
I was ill before the exam and I did ___ (BADLY) out of the whole class.
The ___ (FAR) I've run in one day is about ten kilometres.
Don't you think this would be the ___ (LOVELY) spot for a picnic?
But that's the ___ (CRAZY) idea I've ever heard!
I asked the assistant to show me the ___ (MODERN) phone they had.
I told the manager that it was the ___ (BAD) hotel I had ever stayed in.
Who do you think is the ___ (LITTLE) talented actor to win an Oscar?
Out of all the members of the choir, Jason sang ___ (WELL).

exercises.title: C · Film review
exercises.instruction: Circle the correct word in the film review.

items.prompt: Crime Does Pay, the (1) ___ comedy from director Sam Martin, has to be one of the
little / least interesting films I have ever seen. The acting is terrible and the story is much
(3) ___ than Martin's other flop, Escape.
Crime Does Pay was apparently (4) ___ expensive than any other film this year, but it's hard to see where the money went.
The plot concerns a gang of burglars who decide to steal the (5) ___ valuable painting in the world.
Fine, except these criminals are far (6) ___ amusing than they should be.

When will Hollywood realise that as ticket prices get (9) ___, more people are finding that the
(10) ___ form of entertainment is to spend an evening at home with a DVD?

exercises.title: D · Similar meaning
exercises.instruction: Complete each second sentence using the word given, so that it has a similar meaning to the first. Write between two and five words.

items.prompt:
I have never read a better book than this one. **ever**
This is ___ read.
acceptedAnswers: the best book I have ever

items.prompt:
Nobody has ever been this far into the jungle. **the**
This is ___ has ever been into the jungle.

I have never worked so hard in my whole life. **ever**
It was the ___ in my whole life.

Liam is the tallest boy in the class. **than**
Every other boy in the class ___ Liam.

This is the nicest beach along this part of the coast. **than**
This ___ the others along this part of the coast.

I read that Mount Everest is the highest mountain. **no**
I read that ___ Mount Everest.
acceptedAnswers: no mountain is as high as

items.prompt:
Has anyone ever been this far north before? **the**
Is ___ has ever been?

The painting Ed did is the ugliest one you can imagine. **than**
You can't imagine ___ the one Ed did.

This stamp is rarer than any other in my collection. **more**
The other stamps in my collection ___ this one.

Nobody in the class runs as fast as Pedro. **runner**
Pedro ___ in the class.

exercises.title: E · so … that
exercises.instruction: Rewrite each sentence using so … that.

items.prompt: John can see over the wall because he is tall.
acceptedAnswers: John is so tall that he can see over the wall.
John is so tall he can see over the wall.
John is so tall that he can see over the wall
John is so tall he can see over the wall

items.prompt: I'm sure my sister will go to university because she is clever.
acceptedAnswers: My sister is so clever that I'm sure she will go to university.
My sister is so clever I'm sure she will go to university.
I'm sure my sister is so clever that she will go to university.

items.prompt: I can't stop playing this computer game because it's good.
acceptedAnswers: This computer game is so good that I can't stop playing it.
This computer game is so good I can't stop playing it.
It's so good that I can't stop playing this computer game.

items.prompt: Tim can't come out because he has a lot of work to do.
acceptedAnswers: Tim has so much work to do that he can't come out.
Tim has so much work that he can't come out.
Tim has so much work to do he can't come out.

items.prompt: It's hot, which means I can't sleep.
acceptedAnswers: It's so hot that I can't sleep.
It's so hot I can't sleep.

items.prompt: Tina arrived late, which meant she missed the train.

items.prompt: We don't have any money for luxuries because we have a lot of bills to pay.
acceptedAnswers: We have so many bills to pay that we don't have any money for luxuries.
We have so many bills that we don't have any money for luxuries.

items.prompt: It takes a day to get to Australia because it's very far away.
acceptedAnswers: Australia is so far away that it takes a day to get there.
It's so far away that it takes a day to get to Australia.

exercises.title: G · enough word order

exercises.title: H · Tick or correct
exercises.instruction: If the word in bold is correct, write it again. If it is incorrect, write another word to replace it.

items.prompt: I wanted to get some new trainers but they were **too** expensive.
Japanese is a **too** difficult language for Westerners to learn.
Daniel's **too** good at art and he's starting art school next year.
Don't invite **too** many people to the party or we won't have enough room.
If you try to write your essay **too** quickly, you'll make mistakes.
My new computer is **too** fast and can run all the latest programs.
Joanne was fined for driving **too** fast.
Carol couldn't climb over the wall because it was **too** high.
Cornwall is **too** beautiful and we go there every year on holiday.
My grandparents are **too** old to work now and have retired.
It was **too** dark for me to see the map and I got lost.
My best friend is **too** funny and always makes me laugh.

exercises.title: J · Crimestoppers
exercises.instruction: Write one word in each gap.

items.prompt: Hello, and welcome to Crimestoppers, the show that lets you, the viewer, help the police. We've had ___ a lot of letters this week that it's difficult to know where to begin.
We'll start with the story of Mrs Pat Williams, of Cambridge. Last Friday, Pat decided to go into town with her baby daughter. It's ___ far to walk so they went to the bus stop.
They waited ___ a long time that baby Caroline started to cry.
Pat picked the baby up out of the pram and she was ___ busy she didn't notice the man beside her until it was too late.
He grabbed her handbag and ran off ___ quickly for her to catch him.
It all happened ___ fast that there was nothing anyone could do.
Police are appealing for witnesses. Maybe you were in the area. Maybe you think that what you saw is ___ unimportant that the police won't be interested.
Remember that no detail is ___ small to be useful to the police. Call us here at Crimestoppers now.
